questions.q: Let the vectors& $\overset{→}{u1} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{u2} = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k},$~and~$\overset{→}{u3} = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~be coplanar. If the vectors~$\overset{→}{v1} = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{v2} = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} +  \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$~are also coplanar, then~$6\left(a + b + c\right)& is equal to& $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:& $\overset{→}{u}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{u}2 = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{u}3 = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~are coplanar.

Also given that,$\overset{→}{v}1 = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{v}2 = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$and~$\overset{→}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$~are coplanar.

Now, using the condition of coplanar we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & a \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ c & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding the determinant along~${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(b - 1\right) - \left(1 - c\right) + a \left($1 - bc\right) = 0$

$⇒ a + b + c = 2 + abc . . . . . \left($i\right)$

Again using the coplanar condition we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}$a + b \text{ and } c \text{ and } c \\ a \text{ and } b + c \text{ and } a \\ b \text{ and } b \text{ and } c + a\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Apply row transformations,~ \left({R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - \left({R}_{1} + {R}_{2}\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b & c & c \\ a & b + c & a \\ - 2a & - 2c & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along~${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(a + b\right)\left(0 + 2ac\right) - c\left(0 + 2a^{2}\right) + c\left(-2ac + 2a\left(b + c\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2a^{2}c + 2abc - 2a^{2}c - 2ac^{2} + 2abc + 2ac^{2} = 0$

$⇒ abc = 0$

$∴ a + b + c = 2$~(From eq~ \left($i\right)$)

$∴ 6\left($a + b + c\right) = 12$

Hence this is the correct option.

$

questions.q: Let $A B C D$ be a tetrahedron such that the edges $\mathrm{AB}, \mathrm{AC}$ and AD are mutually perpendicular. Let the areas of the triangles $\mathrm{ABC}, \mathrm{ACD}$ and ADB be 5,6 and 7 square units respectively. Then the area (in square units) of the $\triangle \mathrm{BCD}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\operatorname{Ar}(\triangle B C D)$
$=\sqrt{(\operatorname{Ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC}))^2+(\mathrm{Ar}(\mathrm{ACD}))^2+(\operatorname{Ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ADB}))^2}$
$=\sqrt{5^2+6^2+7^2}$
$=\sqrt{110}$

questions.q: Let a unit vector $\overset{^}{u} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$ make angles $\dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{π}{3}$ and $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ with the vectors $\dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}, \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}$ and $\dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j}$ respectively. If $\overset{→}{v} = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}$, then \(|\hat{u}-\vec{v}|^2\) is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Unit vector $\overset{^}{u} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{p}1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{p}2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{p}3 = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Now angle between $\overset{^}{u}$ and $\overset{→}{p}1 = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$\overset{^}{u} \cdot \overset{→}{p}1 = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{z}{2} = 0$

$⇒ x + z = 0 \ldots \left(i\right)$

Angle between $\overset{^}{u}$ and $\overset{→}{p}2 = $\dfrac{π}{3}

$\overset{^}{u} \cdot \overset{→}{p}2 = | \overset{^}{u} | \cdot \left|\overset{→}{p}2\right|$cos\dfrac{π}{3}

$\overset{^}{u} \cdot \overset{→}{p}2 = $\dfrac{y}{2} + \dfrac{z}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Angle between $\overset{^}{u}$ and $\overset{→}{p}3 = $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}

$\overset{^}{u} \cdot \overset{→}{p}3 = | \overset{^}{u} | \cdot \left|\overset{→}{p}3\right|$cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}

$⇒ $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$⇒ x + y = $\dfrac{- 1}{2} \ldots \left(iii\right)$

from equation (i), (ii) and (iii) we get

$x = \dfrac{- 1}{2},y = 0, z = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus $\overset{^}{u} - \overset{→}{v} = \dfrac{- 1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{^}{u} - \overset{→}{v} = \dfrac{- 2}{2}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j}$

$∴ | \overset{^}{u} - \overset{→}{v}{|}^{2} = \$left(\sqrt{\dfrac{4}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}}\right)$2 = \dfrac{5}{2}$

$

questions.q: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be the vectors of the same magnitude such that $\frac{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|+|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|-|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}=\sqrt{2}+1$. Then $\frac{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|^2}{|\vec{a}|^2}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\frac{|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|+|\bar{a}-\bar{b}|}{|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|-|\bar{a}-\bar{b}|}=\sqrt{2}+1$
Apply componendo and dividendo
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{2|\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}|}{2|\overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{b}}|}=\frac{\sqrt{2}+2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & \Rightarrow|\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}|=(1+\sqrt{2})|\overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{b}}| \\ & \Rightarrow|\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2=(3+2 \sqrt{2})|\overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 2|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2+2 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~b}}=(3+2 \sqrt{2})\left(2|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2-2 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~b}}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 2|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2(2+2 \sqrt{2})=2 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~b}}(4+2 \sqrt{2}) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~b}}}{|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2}=\frac{2+2 \sqrt{2}}{4+2 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$
Now
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{|\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2}{|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2}=1+\frac{|\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2}{|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2}+\frac{2 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~b}}}{|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2} \\ & =1+1+2\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=2+\sqrt{2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$. If $\overset{→}{c}$ is a vector such that $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = | \overset{→}{c} | , | \overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{a} | = 2\sqrt{2}$ and the angle between  \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right)$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ is $\dfrac{π}{6}$, then the value of~\left|\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{c}\right| is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = 3 = a$

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = c$

Now,

\left|\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{a}\right| = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{c} - \overset{→}{a}\right|2 = 8$

$⇒ c^{2} + a^{2} - 2\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{a} = 8$

$⇒ c^{2} + 9 - 2\left(c\right) = 8$

$⇒ c^{2} - 2c + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \left(c - 1\right)2 = 0$

$⇒ c = 1 = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$

Now,

$\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| = \sqrt{{2}^{2} + \left(- 2\right)2 + {1}^{2}} = 3$

Now,

\left|\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right| \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|sin \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)

$⇒ \left|\left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) \times \overset{→}{c}\right| =$3 $\cdot$1 $\cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}

$

questions.q: The sum of the distinct real values of $\mu$ for which the vectors~$\mu\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \mu\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \mu\overset{^}{k}$ are co-planar, is&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given the three vectors are coplanar.

Hence, \left|\begin{cases}\mu & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \mu & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \mu\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \mu\left({μ}^{2} - 1\right) - 1\left(\mu - 1\right) + 1\left(1 - \mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ \mu\left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu + 1\right) - 2 \left(\mu -1\right) = 0 \left[$∵ a^{2} - b^{2} = \left($a - b\right)\left(a + b\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\mu -1\right)\left(\mu\left(\mu +1\right) - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\mu -1\$right)\left({μ}^{2} + \mu +$2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\mu -$1\$right)\left(\mu -$1\right)\left(\mu +2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \mu = 1, 1, - 2$

Therefore, the sum of the distinct real values of $\mu = - 2 + 1 = - 1.

$

questions.q: A vector $\overset{→}{a}$ has components $3p$ and $1$ with respect to a rectangular cartesian system. This system is rotated through a certain angle about the origin in the counter clockwise sense. If, with respect to new system, $\overset{→}{a}$ has components $p + 1$~and $\sqrt{10},$~then a value of $p$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{a}Old = 3p\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{a}New = ( p + 1 ) \overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{10}\overset{^}{j}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a}Old\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}New\right|$

$⇒ 9p^{2} + 1 = p^{2} + 2p + 1 + 10$

$8p^{2} - 2p - 10 = 0$

$4p^{2} - p - 5 = 0$

$( 4p - 5 ) ( p + 1 ) = 0 ⇒ p = \dfrac{5}{4}, - 1$

questions.q: If \left(2, 3, 9\right),  \left(5, 2, 1\right), \left(1, \lambda, 8\right)$ and  \left(\lambda,2, 3\right)$ are coplanar, then the product of all possible values of $\lambda$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Points& $A \left(2, 3, 9\right), B \left($5, 2, 1\right), $C\left($1, \lambda, 8\right) \text{ and } $D\left(\lambda,$2, 3\right)$~are coplanar,

Now we know that condition of coplanarity is \$left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{AB}& \overset{→}{AC} & \overset{→}{AD}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}3 & - 1 & - 8 \\ - 1 & \lambda - 3 & - 1 \\ \lambda - 2 & - 1 & - 6\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ $3\left(\left(-$6\right)\left(\lambda -3\right) - 1\right) + 1\left(6 + \lambda - 2\right) - 8\left(1 - \left(\lambda -3\right)\left(\lambda -2\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(-6\lambda + 17\right) + 4 + \lambda - 8 + 8\left(\lambda -3\$right)\left(\lambda -$2\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 18\lambda + 51 + 4 + \lambda - 8 + 8{λ}^{2} - 40\lambda + 48 = 0$

$⇒ 8{λ}^{2} - 57\lambda + 95 = 0

So product of roots will be~\dfrac{95}{8}

$

questions.q: If the four points, whose position vectors are $3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, - 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $5\overset{^}{i} - 2\alpha\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar, then $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the four points be& $A: ( 3, - 4, 2 )$,~$B: ( 1, 2, - 1 )$, $C: ( - 2, - 1, 3 )$~and~$D: ( 5, - 2\alpha, 4 )$

$A, B, C, D$ are coplanar points, then

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 - 3 & 2 + 4 & - 1 - 2 \\ - 2 - 3 & - 1 + 4 & 3 - 2 \\ 5 - 3 & - 2\alpha + 4 & 4 - 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 6 & - 3 \\ - 5 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & - 2\alpha + 4 & 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ - 3\alpha + 146 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{73}{17}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{^}{a}, \overset{^}{b}$~be unit vectors. If $\overset{→}{c}$~be a vector such that the angle between $\overset{^}{a}$~and $\overset{→}{c}$~is $\dfrac{π}{12}$, and $\overset{^}{b} = \overset{→}{c} + 2 \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right), then \left|$6\overset{→}{c}\right|2$ \text{ and } is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $\overset{^}{b} = \overset{→}{c} + 2 \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right),

$\overset{^}{b} $\cdot \overset{^}{b} = \left(\overset{→}{c} +$2\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)\right) \cdot\left(\overset{→}{c} + 2 \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)\right)

$⇒ 1 = \left(\overset{→}{c} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right) + \overset{→}{c} \cdot$2\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right) +$2\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{c} +$4\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)

$⇒ 1 = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 + 0 + 0 + \left|\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right|$2⇒ 1 = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 + $4\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|2\sin^{2}\dfrac{π}{12}

$⇒ 1 = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 + 4 \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 \left(\dfrac{1 - cos\dfrac{π}{6}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ 1 = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 \left[1 + $2 \left($1 - $\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right]~$⇒ 1 = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|$2 \left[3 - \sqrt{3}\right]$~$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 = \dfrac{1}{3 - \sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{6}$

$∴ 36 \left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 = $\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{6} \times$36 = 6\left(3 + \sqrt{3}\right)$

$

questions.q: If the vectors $\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \mu\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar and the projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on the vector $\overset{→}{b}$ is $\sqrt{54}$ units, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda + \mu$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \mu\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar~

So,~\left|\begin{cases}\lambda & \mu & 4 \\ - 2 & 4 & - 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \lambda ( 10 ) - \mu ( 2 ) + 4 ( - 14 ) = 0$

$⇒ 10\lambda - 2\mu = 56$

$⇒ 5\lambda - \mu = 28 . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And given projection of~$\overset{→}{a}$~on~$\overset{→}{b}$~is~\sqrt{54}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}}{| \overset{→}{b} |} = \sqrt{54}

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 2\lambda + 4\mu - 8}{24} = \sqrt{54}

$⇒ - 2\lambda + 4\mu - 8 = $\sqrt{54 \times 24} . . . . \left(2\right)$

By solving equation~ \left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$~we get,

$⇒ \lambda + \mu = 24$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{\alpha} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{→}{β} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$~If $\overset{→}{β} = \overset{→}{\beta1} - \overset{→}{\beta2},$ where $\overset{→}{\beta1}$ is parallel to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$ and $\overset{→}{\beta2}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{α},$~then $\overset{→}{\beta1} \times \overset{→}{\beta2}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
If two vectors are parallel then they are proportional.

So, let $\overset{→}{{\beta}_{1}} = k\overset{→}{\alpha}$

Given $\overset{→}{\beta} = \overset{→}{{\beta}_{1}} - \overset{→}{{\beta}_{2}}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{α} ⋅ \overset{→}{β} = \overset{→}{α} ⋅ \overset{→}{\beta1} - \overset{→}{α} ⋅ \overset{→}{\beta2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now,~$\overset{→}{α} \cdot \overset{→}{β} = \left($3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)$\cdot \left($2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 6 - 1 = 5$

And,~$\overset{→}{α}$~is perpendicular~to~$\overset{→}{\beta1},$~hence~$\overset{→}{α} ⋅ \overset{→}{\beta1} = 0$

And,~$\overset{→}{α} ⋅ \overset{→}{\beta2} = \overset{→}{α} ⋅ \left($k\overset{→}{α}\right) = $k\left(\overset{→}{α}\right)$2 = $k\left|\overset{→}{α}\right|$2$

Also,~\left|\overset{→}{α}\right| = $\sqrt{{3}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{10}$

Put, all these values in the equation~\left($i\right),$~to get~$5 = k \times10$

$∴ k = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \overset{→}{{\beta}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2} (3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} )$

$= \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Now~$\overset{→}{\beta2} = \overset{→}{\beta1} - \overset{→}{β} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{j} -3\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \overset{→}{\beta1} $\times \overset{→}{\beta2} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ \dfrac{3}{2}& \dfrac{1}{2}& 0 \\ - \dfrac{1}{2}& \dfrac{3}{2}& - 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(- \dfrac{3}{2} -0\right) - \overset{^}{j} \left(- $\dfrac{9}{2} -0\right) + \$overset{^}{k}\$left(\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$= - \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{9}{2}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{5}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} ( -3\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k} ) .$

$

questions.q: Let $a, b$ and~$c$ be distinct positive numbers. If the vectors $a\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $c\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + b\overset{^}{k}$~are co-planar, then $c$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given vectors $a\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $c\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + b\overset{^}{k}$~are co-planar, then

\left|\begin{cases}a & a & c \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ c & c & b\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ a\left(0 - c\right) - a\left(b - c\right) + c\left(c - 0\right) = 0$

$⇒ c^{2} = ab$

$⇒ c = \sqrt{ab} .$

$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ be three distinct real numbers, none equal to one. If the vectors~$a\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$~are coplanar, then~$\dfrac{1}{1 - a} + \dfrac{1}{1 - b} + \dfrac{1}{1 - c}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given that the vectors are coplanar.

That means the determinant is equal to zero.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ {R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} – {R}_{2}$~and~${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} – {R}_{3}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a - 1 & 1 - b & 0 \\ 0 & b - 1 & 1 - c \\ 1 & 1 & c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along~${C}_{1}$.

$⇒ ( a - 1 ) [ c ( b - 1 ) - ( 1 - c ) ] + 1 [ ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) ] = 0$

$⇒ c ( a - 1 ) ( b - 1 ) - ( a - 1 ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) = 0$

$⇒ c ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - b ) + ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) + \left(1 - a\$right)\left(1 - b\right) \left(1 - c\right) = \left(1 - a\right)\left($1 - b\right)\left($1 - c\right)$

$⇒ ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - b ) + ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) = \left($1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right) \left(1 - c\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 - a} + \dfrac{1}{1 - b} + \dfrac{1}{1 - c} =1$

Hence this is the required option.

$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{A}(1,-1,2) \\ & \mathrm{B}(5,7,-6) \\ & \mathrm{C}(3,4,-10) \\ & \mathrm{D}(-1,-4,-2) \\ & \text { Area }=\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{BD}}|=\frac{1}{2}|(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+5 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-12 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times(6 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+11 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{k}})| \\ & =\frac{1}{2}|112 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-64 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-8 \hat{\mathrm{k}}| \\ & =4|14 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-8 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}| \\ & =4 \sqrt{196+64+1} \\ & =4 \sqrt{261} \\ & =12 \sqrt{29}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The sum of all values of $\alpha$, for which the points whose position vectors are~$\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}$~and~$9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$& are coplanar, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the given vectors be& $\overset{→}{A} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{B} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{C} = \left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}and\overset{→}{D} = 9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

We know that if the vectors are coplanar then~\left[\begin{cases}\overset{→}{AB} & \overset{→}{AC} & \overset{→}{AD}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AB} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AC} = \left(\left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AD} = \left(9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 8\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 6\right)\overset{^}{j} + 3k$

Now,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & - 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & 2 & - 1 \\ 8 & \alpha - 6 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(6 + \alpha - 6\right) + \left(3\alpha + 8\right) + \left({α}^{2} - 6\alpha - 16\right) = 0$

On Simplifying we get,

$⇒ {α}^{2} - 2\alpha - 8 = 0$

Therefore, sum of the roots is~$- \left(- 2\right) = 2$.

$

questions.q: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$. Let $\hat{c}$ be a unit vector in the plane of the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ and be perpendicular to $\vec{a}$. Then such a vector $\hat{c}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let vector $\vec{p}$ in plane of $\vec{a} \ \text{ and } \vec{b}=K(\vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b})$
$\begin{aligned}
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \perp \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\lambda \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+\lambda \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 6+\lambda(3)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}=(-3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}})

Unit vector $\rightarrow \pm \frac{(-\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: Let $S$ be the set of all  \left(\lambda, \mu\right)$ for which the vectors~$\lambda\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \mu\overset{^}{k}$~and~$3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$, where~$\lambda - \mu = 5$, are coplanar, then~\mathop{∑}_{ \left(\lambda, \mu\right) \inS}80 \left({λ}^{2} + {μ}^{2}\right)& is& equal to& $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given equations are coplanar.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\lambda & - 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & \mu \\ 3 & - 4 & 5\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \lambda\left[10 + 4\mu\right] + 1\left[5 - 3\mu\right] + 1 \left[-10\right] = 0$

$⇒ 4\lambda\mu + 10\lambda - 3\mu = 5 . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

And~$\lambda - \mu = 5$

So, by~ \left(1\right)$

$⇒ 4\left(5 + \mu\right)\mu + 10\left(5 + \mu\right) - 3\mu = 5$

$⇒ 4{μ}^{2} + 27\mu + 45 = 0$

$⇒ 4{μ}^{2} + 15\mu + 12\mu + 45 = 0$

$∴ \mu = - 3, $\dfrac{- 15}{4}

$⇒ \lambda = 2, $\dfrac{5}{4}

$∴ \mathop{∑}_{\lambda\mu \in S}80 \left({λ}^{2} + {μ}^{2}\right) =80\left[\left($9 + 4\right) + $\dfrac{225}{16} + \dfrac{25}{16}\right]

$= $80\left[$13 + $\dfrac{125}{8}\right] =$10 $\times$229$

$= 2290$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let the plane& $x + 3y - 2z + 6 = 0$~meet the co-ordinate axes at the points~$A, B, C$. If the~orthocenter of the triangle~$ABC$~is~  \left(\alpha, \beta, \dfrac{6}{7}\right)$, then~$98\left(\alpha + \beta\right)2$& is equal to __________.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

The plane& $x + 3y - 2z + 6 = 0$~meet the co-ordinate axes at the points~$A, B, C$,

So,~$A \left(-6, 0, 0\right), B \left($0, - 2, 0\right) \text{ and } $C\left($0, 0, 3\right)$

And the~orthocenter of the triangle~$ABC$~is~\left(\alpha, \beta, \dfrac{6}{7}\right),

We know that, circumcentre of triangle is point of intersection of perpendicular bisectors,

So, plotting the diagram we get,

Now from diagram we can see that~O\text{to midpoint of}$BC ⊥ BC$

So, by perpendicular vector formula we get,

\left(x - 0\right)\times0 + \left(y + 1\right) \times2 + \left(z - $\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \times$3 = 0$

$⇒ 4y + 6z - 5 = 0 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Similarly, for side~$AC$~we get,

\left($x + 3\$right)\times \left(-$6\right) + \left($y - 0\right)\times0 + \left(z - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\left(-3\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4x + 2z + 9 = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left($2\right)$

Similarly, for side~$AB$~we get,

$⇒ \left($x + 3\right)$\times \left(-6\right) + \left(y + 1\right)\times2 + \left($z - 0\right)\times0 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - y + 8 = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left($3\right)$

Now from equation \left(1\right), \left($2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$~we get,

$x = \dfrac{- 9}{4} - \dfrac{z}{2},y = \dfrac{5}{4} - \dfrac{3}{2}z, z = z$

Now using the relation between centroid, circumcentre and orthocentre, we get,

$⇒ G = \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \dfrac{9}{2} - z}{3}, \dfrac{\beta + \dfrac{5}{2} - 3z}{3}, \dfrac{\dfrac{6}{7} + 2z}{3}\right)$

$⇒ \left(-2, - \dfrac{2}{3},1\right) = \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \dfrac{9}{2} - z}{3}, \dfrac{\beta + \dfrac{5}{2} - 3z}{3}, \dfrac{\dfrac{6}{7} + 2z}{3}\right)$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$⇒ z = \dfrac{15}{14}, \alpha = - \dfrac{3}{7}, \beta = - \dfrac{9}{7}$

$⇒ 98\left(\alpha + \beta\right)2 = 98 \times \dfrac{144}{49} =288$

$
